copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Belgium v IR Iran in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Sunday, and the model and the market disagree on the IR Iran side by +14.8pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

The Elo prior reads Belgium 1860 vs IR Iran 1740: 120 points in favour of Belgium, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Belgium to win at 51%, the draw at 23%, and IR Iran to win at 26%. The Desk publishes a three-way read against the same W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on — not a scoreline guess. IR Iran sits at 26% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Belgium to win at 68%, the draw at 21%, and IR Iran to win at 11%. Polymarket has IR Iran at 11%, which prices out at American odds of +809; the model has the same side at 26%. The +14.8pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

The +3pp Pick threshold isn't on the point estimate, it's on the 5th-percentile from a 100-sample bootstrap of the Elo prior plus bonuses. On IR Iran, that haircut lands the model at 21%; the market is at 11%. Even on the conservative reading, the gap is +10.0pp. The point is selection, not a blanket call. Most matches the model and the market agree on. This is one of the ones where they don't, and the gap is on the IR Iran side specifically.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 30 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.
drivers: Bootstrap lower-bound on the IR Iran side still clears the Pick threshold.
Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades or recommend a wager.
Pre-match Elo gives IR Iran a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +14.8pp gap clears the Desk's 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
copy.summary: A +14.8pp gap across model and market on the IR Iran side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates IR Iran at 26%; Polymarket sits at 11%.
